items: Made a classic French onion soup: caramelized onions for 45 minutes, beef broth, thyme, Gruyere croutons. The slow caramelization is key — no shortcuts.
Sourdough starter day 7: finally getting consistent rise. Fed twice daily at 1:1:1 ratio. Smells tangy and sweet. Ready for first loaf tomorrow.
Blind tasting of olive oils: Italian was fruity and peppery, Spanish was milder, Greek was robust. The peppery finish on the Italian won for salad dressing.
Knife skills practice: brunoise, julienne, chiffonade. Proper knife technique is faster and safer than rushing with bad form. Sharp knife = safe knife.
Fermented hot sauce batch 3: habaneros, garlic, salt, 2-week ferment. pH dropped to 3.4. Blended with vinegar. Much better depth than store-bought.
Pasta dough ratio: 100g flour per egg, pinch of salt, drizzle of olive oil. Knead 10 minutes, rest 30. Roll to setting 6 on the machine for tagliatelle.
Smoked brisket for 14 hours at 225°F. Hit the stall at 160°F for 3 hours. Wrapped in butcher paper to push through. Internal temp 203°F before resting.
Learned the mother sauces: béchamel, velouté, espagnole, hollandaise, tomato. Every classic sauce derives from these five. Mastering them unlocks hundreds of variations.
Bread baking: autolyse technique — mix flour and water, rest 30 minutes before adding yeast and salt. Gluten development starts passively. Less kneading needed.
Thai green curry from scratch: mortar and pestle for the paste — galangal, lemongrass, green chilies, shrimp paste, cilantro root. Night and day vs jarred paste.
Temperature control for steak: reverse sear method. Oven at 275°F until internal 120°F, then cast iron sear at maximum heat. Perfect edge-to-edge medium-rare.
Preserved lemons: packed in salt and lemon juice, aged 30 days. The rind becomes soft and intensely flavored. Essential for Moroccan tagines.
Chocolate tempering: seed method. Melt to 115°F, add seed chocolate while stirring, bring down to 82°F, then back up to 88-90°F. Snap and shine.
Ramen broth: 18-hour simmer of pork bones. Cloudy tonkotsu requires vigorous rolling boil to emulsify the collagen. Clear chintan needs gentle simmer.
Mise en place practice: measured and prepped every ingredient before turning on the stove. Cooking became calm and controlled instead of chaotic.
Croissant dough: 3-day process. Day 1: détrempe. Day 2: lamination — 3 single folds with butter block. Day 3: shape, proof, bake at 400°F.
Wok technique: heat until smoking, small amount of high-smoke-point oil, ingredients in stages by cooking time. Toss constantly. Wok hei comes from extreme heat.
Coffee extraction: 18g beans, 36g output, 25-30 seconds. Grind finer if sour (under-extracted), coarser if bitter (over-extracted). Water at 200°F.
Fermented vegetables: salt at 2% of vegetable weight, submerge in brine, room temp 3-5 days. Lactobacillus does the work. No vinegar needed.
Sushi rice: 1.1 ratio water to rice. Rice vinegar, sugar, salt for seasoning. Fan while folding — shininess comes from rapid cooling. Never refrigerate.
Stock vs broth: stock uses bones (collagen = body), broth uses meat (flavor). Roast bones first for brown stock. Simmer gently — boiling makes it cloudy.
Butter clarification: melt slowly, skim foam, pour off golden fat leaving milk solids. Ghee goes further — brown the solids for nutty flavor before straining.
Bread scoring patterns: controls oven spring direction. Score at 45° angle for ear. Depth matters — too shallow and it tears, too deep and it deflates.
Fermentation temperature: 75-78°F ideal for most cultures. Too cold and nothing happens. Too hot and off-flavors develop. Proof box or oven with light on.
Ice cream base: custard method with egg yolks for richness. Cook to 170°F — any hotter and you get scrambled eggs. Strain, chill overnight, churn.
